summary: Franklin County, NY fire lookout on Mount Morris near Tupper Lake: 22-ft steel tower finished 1919, lookout ended 1971; now closed, ownership disputed, condition unverified.

facts.design: 22-foot steel Aermotor LS40 fire lookout tower
facts.status_note: Two lists say it remains; no recent description of its condition was found

access.note: Remains on private property and is closed to the public, per the NYSFFLA list; Wikipedia also says closed to the public. Sources disagree on who owns it.

facts.agency: New York State: Forest, Fish and Game Commission, later the State Conservation Department

events.note: Lookout established on the summit at a cost of $924.84; Wikipedia says no tower was needed because the view was already open
Tower construction completed; Wikipedia gives 1919 and an Aermotor LS40 model
A new cabin was erected at the station
Fire warden on duty at the tower; volunteers searched the mountain that June for a missing six-year-old
Vandals destroyed telephone and radio equipment at the summit in April; replacements had to be packed up on foot
Fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1971 season as aerial detection increased

In January the tower was described as abandoned and declared state surplus; the Town of Altamont board voted unanimously to submit a bid, and the town's offer was $1. Wikipedia says ownership later passed to the town of Altamont (late 1970s)

corrections.proposed: New York State: Forest, Fish and Game Commission, later the State Conservation Department
corrections.why: The value is the first date line of the source's timeline, not an agency name. The page names the state Forest, Fish and Game Commission (1910 report) and the State Conservation Department (1957).
That name belongs to the Manhattan watchtower in Marcus Garvey Park, which has its own record (us-ny-harlem-fire-watchtower). This Franklin County lookout is a different tower.

corrections.current: 2019 restored (historic fire watchtower in Marcus Garvey Park, Harlem)
corrections.why: The 2019 restoration and reopening were of the Harlem tower. The NYSFFLA project was matched to this record by name and given its coordinates.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives the mountain as 3,117 feet; the Forest Lookouts page gives 3,163 feet. The story reports both rather than choosing one.
The FFLA list and the NYSFFLA list both say the tower remains. Neither gives its present condition. The 1976 surplus notice is history, not a current status.
Wikipedia says ownership passed to the town in the late 1970s; the NYSFFLA list says it remains on private property. Not resolved from the sources read.
Forest Lookouts says the steel tower was bought in 1918 and finished in 1919; Wikipedia gives 1919 as the build year. These agree on the completion date.
Forest Lookouts says a lookout was established in July 1909 at a cost; Wikipedia says the station was built without a tower because the view was already open. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The us-ny-mount-morris record merges two towers. The Manhattan Mount Morris watchtower in Harlem (Marcus Garvey Park) has its own record, us-ny-harlem-fire-watchtower. The 2019 restored event and the 'Mount Morris Fire Watchtower, Harlem' other name belong to that tower. The nysffla_projects row for the Harlem tower carries the Franklin County coordinates (44.15976, -74.47517) because it was matched to this record by name; fix the matching as well as this record. The 22-foot (6.7 m) height and 1919 completion are consistent across Wikipedia and Forest Lookouts. Ownership and current condition remain unresolved: a state or town records check, or a recent site report, would settle them. Access is recorded as closed, so do not encourage a climb. No new photos were added.
